Subacius Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Panevėžio apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. Old Subacius's Jewish cemetery carried the local nickname 'Paris,' after a small neighboring village called Paryzius. The town's five-generations-deep Jewish community split when a new railway station drew the town's center of gravity to a new township nearby in the 1870s, with the larger part of the community, including the rabbi, relocating there. The remaining Old Subacius families were further reduced when the Russian army drove most of them out during WWI. This cemetery, dating to the end of the 18th century, was recently documented in full with help from volunteers at the Subacius secondary school.
